query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Engineering a heterogeneous grain structure in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy through processing or synthesis route will increase its load-bearing integrity while preserving its caloric performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
generation.intervention: Heterogeneous grain structure engineering through processing or synthesis route
generation.mechanism: The heterogeneous grain structure will impede dislocation motion, induce strengthening, and enhance ductility, leading to improved load-bearing integrity. The low stacking fault energy of the alloy will facilitate the generation of twinned nanograins and stacking faults during tensile straining, dynamically reinforcing the heterogeneity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased load-bearing integrity and preserved caloric performance
generation.baseline: Current (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with poor load-bearing integrity and tendency to crack
generation.boundary: Operating temperatures and pressures within the range of applied-field and pressure-field operation
generation.uncertainty: The exact extent of improvement in load-bearing integrity and preservation of caloric performance is uncertain and requires experimental verification

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile testing and caloric performance measurement of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with engineered heterogeneous grain structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the engineered alloy shows no significant improvement in load-bearing integrity (tensile strength and ductility) or a significant degradation in caloric performance, the hypothesis is falsified.

Here we examine a variant of the single-phase CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy in which two of the elements have been removed. The resulting CrCoNi alloy, an equiatomic ‘medium-entropy alloy' (MEA), has a single-phase, fcc crystal structure, whose uniaxial tensile properties have recently been reported. The experimental results (X-ray diffraction and backscattered electron, BSE, images) are consistent with the CrCoNi ternary phase diagrams, which indicate that the equiatomic composition is a single-phase solid solution at elevated temperatures. (XRD and BSE analyses of the five-component CrMnFeCoNi alloy after casting and homogenization showed that it too is single-phase fcc and remains so after recrystallization when examined by transmission electron microscopy. SignificanceBack stress hardening is usually not obvious in single-phase homogeneous grains, but can be made unusually large and sustained to large tensile strains by creating an unusually heterogeneous grain structure in single-phase alloys with low stacking fault energy (SFE), as demonstrated here for the face-centered cubic CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy. The low SFE facilitates the generation of twinned nanograins and stacking faults during tensile straining, dynamically reinforcing the heterogeneity. decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has focused on improving their mechanical properties, such as strength, ductility, and toughness, through various methods like alloying, processing, and surface engineering. Recent studies have explored the effects of interstitial elements, like N and C, on the stacking fault energy of medium-entropy alloys, which can lead to enhanced strength and strain hardening. Additionally, the development of heterogeneous grain structures and the introduction of reinforcements, such as SiC particles, have been shown to improve the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
decision.unsolved: The poor load-bearing integrity and tendency to crack of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy under applied-field and pressure-field operation remain unsolved. The current research has not fully addressed the relationship between the alloy's composition, microstructure, and mechanical properties, particularly under extreme conditions.
decision.why: Based on the trend of research on high-entropy alloys, engineering a heterogeneous grain structure in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy could potentially improve its load-bearing integrity and reduce its tendency to crack. This approach has been shown to enhance the mechanical properties of other high-entropy alloys, and its application to this specific alloy could lead to improved performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
